extracted.intended_audience: Members of the British Government / Board of Control and the Court of Directors of the East India Company (officials administering Indian affairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts of official representations and correspondence setting rules and objections about the settlement of the Nabob of Arcot's private debts, the application of the twelve lacs of pagodas fund, and the permitted conduct of Company servants in financial and personal interactions with native rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Company servants engaging in loans with country powers
rubrics_metrics.description: “no person, being a servant of the Company, or being under our protection, shall, on any pretence whatever, be concerned in any loan or other money transaction with any of the country powers, unless with the knowledge and express permission of our respective governments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations are to be strictly dealt with: offenders discovered counteracting these orders are to be sent home to England to be punished as guilty of disobedience of orders; no protection or assistance of the Company shall be given for the recovery of any loans connected with such transactions. Particular attention is enjoined and any connivance will incur the highest displeasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob and his family
rubrics_metrics.description: “we repeat our prohibition in the strongest terms respecting any intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob and his family; as we are convinced that such an intercourse has been carried on greatly to the detriment and expense of the Nabob, and merely to the advantage of individuals.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs that all persons who offend against the letter and spirit of this order, whether in the Company's service or under their protection, be forthwith sent to England. Presented as necessary to put an end to intrigues carried on at the Nabob's durbar.

rubrics_metrics.name: No company assistance for recovery of loans made contrary to orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If any servant or person under protection is concerned in forbidden loans, “no protection or assistance of the Company shall be given for the recovery of any loans connected with such transactions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a deterrent: such transactions not only subject the actor to punishment but also remove any Company support for debt recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company's claim to priority of arrears from the twelve lacs fund
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court asserts its right to be paid the arrears of those expenses by which, almost to our own ruin, we have preserved the country ... surely stands paramount to all claims for former debts upon the revenues of a country so preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct implication that until the Company's debt is discharged it will not consent to give up any part of the seven lacs (allocated to it by treaty) to private creditors; framed as an assertion of rights and precedence over private creditors in allocation of the fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to question the justice of debts must be preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: “the opportunity of questioning, within the limited time, the justice of any of the debts, ought to have been fully preserved;”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court objects to amendments that would preclude adequate examination; argues that inquiry into the justice of debts cannot injure individuals and should be fully preserved within the statutory timetable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry into the nature, origin, and rate of interest of debts
rubrics_metrics.description: The act expressly directed examination of the nature and origin of the debts; the Court questions whether the amended paragraphs comply and whether “the rate of interest, according to which the debts arising from soucar assignment of the land-revenues ... have been accumulated, ought not to be inquired into.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically calls for investigation into how high interest may have been charged and into the reasonableness of a 25% deduction directed by the Bengal government from many debts; implies that such inquiries affect fairness of relief to private creditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debts to be computed with simple interest (not compound)
rubrics_metrics.description: “This it was not our intention to allow; and lest any misconception should arise on the spot, we have added an express direction that the debts be made up with simple interest only, from the time of their respective consolidation. Clause F f.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners instruct that, contrary to some local computations, compound interest at differing rates is not to be allowed — simple interest only from consolidation date. This is an explicit computational/legal standard for totaling debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: If revenue deficiency arises, payments made proportionately as originally divided
rubrics_metrics.description: “if, notwithstanding the provisions contained in our former paragraphs, any deficiency should arise, the payments of what shall be received shall be made in the same proportion which would have obtained in the division of the whole twelve lacs, had they been paid.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners direct that any shortfall in receipts should be shared in the originally-prescribed proportions among classes of claimants rather than falling wholly on any one class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use best available local revenue estimates when assessing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioners place reliance on the estimate transmitted by the President of Fort St. George, “having there the best means of information upon the fact, and stating it with a particular view to the subject matter of these paragraphs.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance that central decision-makers should rely on the most informed local assessments in revenue estimations and not accept less-informed lower estimates that might reduce perceived benefits of a plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of balancing expediency, justice, and humanity in debt settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioners argue the arrangement is defensible not only on expediency (reestablishing credit and circulation) but also for motives of attention to feelings and honor of the Nabob, of humanity to individuals, and of justice to persons in your service and living under your protection, which have actuated the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents a normative framework for judging policy: include practical economic expediency, reparation of honor, humanitarian concerns, and justice to Company servants when arranging settlement schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity to investigate serious accusations and to protect honest governors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where letters charge ‘enormous crimes, and corruptions of the grossest kind, on a British governor,’ the Commissioners note it is necessary to inquire into their truth or falsehood so as to 'protect the honest fame of virtuous governors as it is to punish the corrupt and tyrannical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for inquiry into such charges; if proved, censure the accused; if forged, censure the accuser; underlines need for proper measures to secure government against infamous accusations and to maintain public confidence.
